claims.claim_text: ASTS has a federal contract with the U.S. Space Development Agency (SDA) — including a $43.0M contract via a prime contractor for testing services using the initial BB satellites, plus a direct $30.0M SDA Europa Track 2 commercial-solutions contract, plus an IDIQ award under the Missile Defense Agency's SHIELD program.

ASTS has definitive commercial agreements with AT&T (space-based wireless connectivity for the U.S.) and Verizon (definitive commercial agreement announced October 8, 2025 for direct-to-cellular service starting 2026), plus an existing AT&T agreement and strategic investments.

ASTS claims an intellectual-property portfolio of approximately 3,850 patent and patent-pending claims covering direct-to-cell satellite ecosystem (large phased array, beamforming, ASIC chip AST5000).

ASTS has 5 Block 1 BB satellites in orbit (launched September 12, 2024) and launched its first Block 2 BB satellite (BB6) on December 23, 2025 — i.e. 6 commercial BB satellites in orbit at cutoff, with claimed near-term plans to initiate limited noncontinuous SpaceMobile service.

ASTS operates satellite assembly, integration and test (AIT) facilities in Texas (Midland) headquartered there, plus engineering/production centers in Florida (Homestead), Maryland (Lanham), Spain, Israel, India, and Scotland — global footprint approximately 450,000 sq ft.

ASTS reports $2.8 billion of cash and restricted cash at 12/31/2025 (up from $567.5M at 12/31/2024), reported FY2025 net loss before NCI of approximately $461M; SpaceMobile Service has not been launched and has generated zero service revenue; risk factor explicitly references potential future going-concern qualifier. ASTS has a long history of heavily dilutive financings.

Ten-year commercial agreement with Saudi Telecom Company (STC, October 29, 2025) for direct-to-device satellite mobile connectivity across Saudi Arabia and key regional markets; plus reseller agreement with jointly-owned European 'SatCo' Vodafone JV (December 18, 2025).

ASTS claims agreements with 'multiple launch vehicle providers' to secure launch contracts for the planned Block 2 BB constellation rollout. No specific named launch provider, vehicle name, or named launch site (Vandenberg/Cape Canaveral/Wallops) is given in Item 1.

kwargs.q: BlueBird Block 2 launch SpaceX Blue Origin
